exception.reason: The strongest direction—Korean language, literature and cultural media—was tested before history/society and regional politics/economic-development directions. UCR has useful disciplinary methods in literature, film, media, heritage, history, sociology, politics, international relations and economics. The current catalogue nevertheless contains no Korean-language course and no documented Korea-specific course sequence. Because Korean language, Korean sources and sustained study of Korea are the organising substance of the external curriculum, a 23-course non-PPD programme assembled from generic methods would change the object of study rather than provide a related complete response. The history/society direction lacks Korean historical, social and division content; the politics/development direction lacks Korea- or East Asia-centred political economy. The outcome is based on complete-programme coherence and course content, not title matching, exact module equivalence or professional qualification.
exception.curriculumContext: The settled current Korean Studies pathway remains complete at 180 EC. It preserves 65 EC of selected Korean language and reading study, Korea-specific history, culture, politics and digital/topical work, a 5-EC thesis seminar followed by the 10-EC final paper, and 30 EC of genuine open choice. Themes and Approaches remains 10 EC under the current group and module; Korean 3 and Business Korean are the selected prerequisite-feasible options. No route is invented and no first-stage curriculum decision is reopened.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 rows in the current enriched UCR workbook, including descriptions or outline-derived profiles, prerequisites and the six cohort availability columns. MCCLITR111, MCCLITR211 and MCCLITR312 teach literary interpretation, world myth and critical perspectives; MCCMEDI111, MCCMEDI212, MCCMEDI311 and MCCMEDI312 teach film/media form, postcolonial or race-aware representation and documentary methods. Those are substantive methods but are not documented Korean literature, K-pop/K-drama, Korean cultural tradition or Korean media study. MCCHEAM112 is world archaeology with examples in Türkiye, Sudan, the classical Mediterranean, the Harappan Valley and the Philippines; MCCHEAM211 is West African art/heritage. Neither establishes Korean material heritage. GOSHIST111 surveys modern history with a mainly European/international chronology and a decolonisation component; GOSHIST211 treats empires comparatively; GOSHIST312 researches the Walcheren Expedition; none supplies Korean history or the peninsula division. GOSSOCI111/214 provide sociology shaped by colonial critique, GOSSOCI212 qualitative methods and GOSSOCI311 global civil-society theory with Latin American and European cases, not sustained Korean society. GOSPOLI112, GOSPOLI212 and GOSPOLI313 provide comparative-politics, international-relations and peace/conflict frameworks; BENECON111 and BENECON211 provide general economics and international macroeconomics. Their actual content does not teach Korean politics, North/South Korea or Korean economic development. HCBCOGN312 studies psycholinguistics, bilingualism and acquisition but is not language instruction; MCCCOMM112 is Dutch. No workbook row teaches Korean, Korean reading/writing or an East Asia/Korea area-studies spine. Academic feasibility therefore fails before accepting 24 courses, so no schedule or UCR-credit comparison is fabricated.

candidateAssessment.concept: Korean language, literature and cultural media
candidateAssessment.assessment: UCR supplies literary, film, media, rhetoric and heritage methods, but no Korean-language instruction and no documented Korean literature, media, cultural tradition or material-heritage sequence. Filling 23 non-PPD places with generic methods would remove the Korean object that defines the direction.

candidateAssessment.concept: Korean history, society and the divided peninsula
candidateAssessment.assessment: Modern history, empire, sociology and qualitative methods are genuine analytic foundations, but the documented course content does not provide Korean history, the division of the peninsula, North Korean communism, South Korean capitalism or sustained social-science study of Korea.

candidateAssessment.concept: Korea in regional politics and economic development
candidateAssessment.assessment: Comparative politics, international relations and international macroeconomics supply transferable frameworks. They do not offer a Korea- or East Asia-centred politics and development sequence, so expanding them to a full programme would become generic international studies rather than a defensible response to the stated Korean Studies interest.
